rows.title: Xcel customers face increasing outages and are waiting longer for support. “We have a real problem,” regulators say.
rows.standfirst: Blackouts are becoming longer and more common in Xcel’s Colorado service territory, with 90,000 customers experiencing 6 or more outages in 2024

rows.title: Are most homes in Denver made of brick?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Just over half of all homes in Denver are made of brick or brick-composite materials, the result of a code enacted after an 1863 fire.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s imports and exports to China continue to drop in 2025
rows.standfirst: Is that going to impact the state’s GDP too? Maybe, say economists. Plus: Why Colorado job openings are up, Denver restaurant numbers are flat, Charter’s employee stock perk, strike avoided and more!

rows.title: The big bills Colorado’s legislature has to deal with before the 2025 lawmaking term ends Wednesday
rows.standfirst: The big union bill, a resolution forcing a lawsuit aimed at dismantling the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights and Gov. Jared Polis signature housing measure are all still pending with just 5 days left in Colorado’s 2025 legislative session

rows.title: Colorado union and business leaders can’t reach deal on Labor Peace Act, so Democrats will test Jared Polis’ veto pen
rows.standfirst: The governor has said he opposes any effort to repeal a requirement that workers get to vote on whether they should be forced to pay fees for collective bargaining representation — whether or not they are members of their workplace’s union

rows.title: Could Trump actually revive Colorado’s vilified coal industry?
rows.standfirst: Many state mines will close when their nearby power plant stops burning the carbon fuel, but others could export more, experts say

rows.title: Ski train to Steamboat looking likely under new mountain railroad agreement
rows.standfirst: Gov. Jared Polis announced Colorado’s new deal with Union Pacific, calling for three passenger trips per day on mountain rail

rows.title: Attempt to tweak Colorado’s controversial, first-in-the-nation artificial intelligence law is killed
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 318 was tabled after consensus on the tweaks couldn’t be reached between the tech industry, consumer advocates and lawmakers. Colorado’s first-in-the nation AI law goes into effect Feb. 1, 2026.

rows.title: Colorado has a checkered history with pro cycling road races. But a British company thinks it can succeed here.
rows.standfirst: UK-based Infinity Events Group announced plans to launch a world-class men’s stage race in Colorado beginning in September 2026.

rows.title: Colorado added 48,600 new businesses in the first quarter, but lost about 17,000
rows.standfirst: In an uncertain economy, business filings tell a different story about operating in uncertain times

rows.title: Legislature rejects Jared Polis’ key effort this year to drive down Colorado home insurance costs
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1302 would have imposed a 1% fee on every homeowners insurance policy. Homeowners would have borne the cost, which is why the measure died.

rows.title: Colorado Senate rejects “YIGBY” measure, a priority for Jared Polis that would have boosted housing on church land
rows.standfirst: The measure, House Bill 1169, would have overridden local zoning laws, escalating a long-running dispute between the state and local governments over housing policy

rows.title: Jeffco “clean iron” plant gets inaugural $8 million Colorado decarbonization tax credit
rows.standfirst: The industrial tax credits are aimed at pushing the state toward 50% emissions cuts by 2030

rows.title: MSU Denver students beat the market in investment class — using real money
rows.standfirst: Two student-managed funds have performed 20 percentage points better than the Russell 3000 since the funds’ inception in 2020. But 2025 has been more challenging and student funds had mixed results.

rows.title: 101 bills debated by the Colorado legislature in 2025 that you need to know about
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Capitol News Alliance pored through the more than 600 measures debated at the Capitol this year to highlight the most notable ones that passed and failed

rows.title: Jared Polis plans to veto Labor Peace Act bill, a priority for Colorado unions
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 5 would abolish a requirement in the Colorado Labor Peace Act that 75% of workers at a company sign off before unions can negotiate with businesses over union security. That’s after a majority of workers vote to unionize.

rows.title: Are beer and wine sales in Colorado grocery chains hurting small liquor stores?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Small liquor stores in Colorado saw sharp drops in sales after the state allowed beer and wine sales in large grocery chains.

rows.title: Special legislative session on Colorado’s AI law looms after lawmakers failed to act
rows.standfirst: Tech companies warn that the law, which is scheduled to go into effect Feb. 1, 2026, would stifle innovation in Colorado and impose an administrative burden on any businesses that use AI

rows.title: What’s Working: Could an army of young conservationists fill a firefighting gap in Colorado?
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s eight conservation service corps help prevent wildfires, build trails and eradicate invasive species — all for an average $500 a week.

rows.title: Colorado’s largest community built from shipping containers is providing a housing road map
rows.standfirst: A first-time developer navigated complicated and pricey approvals to build a 16-unit complex in downtown Buena Vista built with steel shipping containers

rows.title: Weld County oil well blowout exposed people miles away to high levels of benzene, researchers say
rows.standfirst: The chemical plume from Chevron’s Bishop pad in tiny Galeton flowed for almost five days in April before the well was secured and sealed

rows.title: National Trust for Local News sheds Colorado papers, will continue to operate printing press
rows.standfirst: Arizona-based Times Media Group will take 21 titles, many employees and contribute page design, ad sales and circulation support to remaining Colorado Community Media papers

rows.title: Meat processor Cargill builds workforce housing in Fort Morgan in 10 months
rows.standfirst: With new townhouses open and apartments coming on line this autumn, the work commutes of hundreds of employees will drastically shortened

rows.title: A new era of single-stair apartment buildings is coming to Denver and other Colorado cities
rows.standfirst: Under House Bill 1273, cities with more than 100,000 residents must revise their building codes by Dec. 1, 2027, to allow for a single stairway exit in apartment buildings of up to five stories, with a maximum of four units to a floor

rows.title: Denver is starting to see results from COVID-era investments in housing for people who are homeless
rows.standfirst: In the span of about two weeks, the metro area is celebrating “ready-to-work” housing in Englewood, a family hotel on Colfax, and an affordable apartment complex in southwest Denver

rows.title: Xcel says it has moved to solve service problems. Colorado regulators want to verify the progress.
rows.standfirst: Hoping to reverse a trend that included unresolved billing problems and long power outages, Xcel has hired 170 agents and plans to add more

rows.title: Historic Stanley Hotel sells to unique partnership led by Colorado state cultural authority
rows.standfirst: The sale — funded by a $400 million public bond offering — will help fund an expansion of the historic hotel and a new events center that could host part of the Sundance Film Festival

rows.title: Jared Polis will withhold state grants to Colorado cities, counties that don’t comply with new housing laws
rows.standfirst: The governor issued an executive order Friday requiring local governments to show they’re enacting policies to encourage more housing in order to qualify for transportation and energy funds.

rows.title: Jared Polis vetoes Colorado labor movement’s priority bill. Union leaders say they’ll be back.
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 5 would have abolished a requirement in the Colorado Labor Peace Act that 75% of workers at a company sign off before unions can negotiate with businesses over union security. That’s after a majority of workers vote to unionize.

rows.title: What’s Working: After a Colorado law required employers to add a retirement plan, a local chamber built its own
rows.standfirst: Behind Colorado Springs Chamber’s 401(k)s plan for multiple employers. Plus: Local retirement plans, laws impacting seniors, 4.8% jobless rate, more!

rows.title: The future of federal rental assistance in Colorado is highly uncertain
rows.standfirst: Rental assistance programs could be completely overhauled if President Donald Trump’s “skinny budget” is passed without amendment.

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers OK $67M for water programs, cut tax break for free sports bets
rows.standfirst: Other measures include new rules for mine cleanup and water quality, and new rules for use of nonfunctional turf

rows.title: How financial scams work — and how to avoid them
rows.standfirst: The easiest way to keep a bad actor from hooking you is to remember, it’s fine not to reply to a text or call asking for money

rows.title: Cryptocurrency ATMs target the “unbanked” in Colorado. So do scammers.
rows.standfirst: A bill awaiting Gov. Polis’ signature could help stave off financial crimes that target the most vulnerable individuals

rows.title: Colorado cities sue Jared Polis, state over housing policies
rows.standfirst: A lawsuit filed Monday argues the state is violating the right of local governments to shape how they grow and develop

rows.title: Jets are carrying passengers from Pueblo to Denver again. For now.
rows.standfirst: Essential Air Service subsidies that support service to three rural Colorado airports, including Pueblo, are targeted in the 2026 “skinny budget”

rows.title: AT&T buying Lumen’s home fiber business, including Colorado market, for $5.75 billion
rows.standfirst: Coloradans may be more familiar with Lumen’s old moniker, CenturyLink. The company will take over 1 million Quantum Fiber customers.

rows.title: Can renters in Colorado be required to earn more than double their rent?
rows.standfirst: No. Landlords in Colorado may require tenants to make up to 200% of their annual rent, but they cannot lawfully require more than that.

rows.title: Revise, delay or implement? The standoff over Colorado’s artificial intelligence discrimination law
rows.standfirst: Business and industry groups have been begging for a delay. They say the law as it stands is unworkable — they’re urging Colorado’s lawmakers to give all sides more time to try to find a compromise.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado restaurant owners spoke out to change state policy this year. It worked, sorta.
rows.standfirst: It hasn’t yet helped restaurants still struggling with higher costs but attention to their plight seemed like progress, they say. Plus: Denver’s budget problems, upcoming job fairs, more!

rows.title: Multiple wolf attacks reported on ranches near Aspen over Memorial Day weekend
rows.standfirst: Three ranches near where wolves were released in January say Colorado Parks and Wildlife is not keeping its promise to let them know when the collared animals are near

rows.title: Xcel’s $30M plan to join regional “power pool” panned for high cost, lack of benefit
rows.standfirst: Xcel Energy must join wholesale electric market to meet Colorado law. Execs say big upfront cost is best economic and operational choice.

rows.title: Mushroom startups ready themselves for Colorado’s untested psilocybin healing industry
rows.standfirst: Regulators worked to keep the barriers to entry low, yet new healing businesses face challenges in a highly restricted market

rows.title: Uinta Basin Railway supported with U.S. Supreme Court ruling that may push more crude through Colorado
rows.standfirst: The high court ruled against environmental groups and Eagle County, agreeing that the Surface Transportation Board’s 2021 review of the 88-mile rail line in Utah was appropriate under the National Environmental Policy Act

rows.title: Jared Polis vetoes bill that would have restricted the use of rent-setting software, like RealPage
rows.standfirst: Rent-setting algorithms have become a target of consumer protection advocates in recent years, who say they effectively enable landlords to collude and drive up the cost of housing

rows.title: Colorado’s quantum Tech Hub partners with IBM to train 3,500 workers
rows.standfirst: It’s part of a federally-funded workforce development effort by Elevate Quantum, but this piece won’t cost the organization a dime.

rows.title: Colorado landfills generate as much dirty air as driving 1 million cars for a year
rows.standfirst: Proposed rules would force operators to measure methane emissions, fix leaks and, in some cases, install gas collection systems.

rows.title: Gross Reservoir dam construction can resume, but federal judge says key environmental permits must be redone
rows.standfirst: The ruling calls into question how much water can be diverted from the Colorado River system to fill the reservoir owned by Denver Water

rows.title: What’s Working: When the wind blows in Blanca, the brisk business of sand slides in
rows.standfirst: Dust storms translate into sales for a small business owner who’s dreaming of expanding to regenerative recreation equipment. Plus: Insurance discounts for disaster mitigation, tax incentives for rural businesses, more!
